items.q: A lung biopsy from a patient with chronic cough and weight loss shows necrotising granulomas with amorphous granular debris at the centre. Which feature best defines this central change?
items.exp: Central amorphous necrosis inside a granuloma is caseous necrosis, classic for tuberculosis. The necrotic centre loses all cellular detail, unlike coagulative necrosis where outlines persist.
r: Incorrect. Coagulative necrosis preserves outlines and typifies ischaemic infarction.
Correct. Amorphous central debris in a granuloma is caseous necrosis.
Incorrect. Liquefactive necrosis forms pus in pyogenic infection and brain infarction.
Incorrect. Fat necrosis follows pancreatic enzyme release or breast trauma.
items.kp: Caseation inside a granuloma points first to tuberculosis.

items.q: Which cell is the central orchestrator of chronic inflammation and granuloma formation?
items.exp: Macrophages organise chronic inflammation, present antigen, secrete cytokines and fuse into giant cells within granulomas. Neutrophils dominate acute inflammation instead.
r: Incorrect. Neutrophils dominate early acute inflammation.
Correct. Activated macrophages organise chronic inflammation and granulomas.
Incorrect. Mast cells mediate allergy and early vascular changes.
Incorrect. Platelets drive haemostasis, not granuloma structure.
items.kp: Think macrophage whenever chronic inflammation is asked.

items.q: A giant cell in a granuloma shows nuclei arranged around the periphery in a horseshoe pattern. What is this cell called?
items.exp: Langhans giant cells, formed by macrophage fusion, arrange nuclei at the periphery. Foreign body giant cells scatter nuclei randomly through the cytoplasm.
r: Incorrect. Foreign body cells scatter nuclei randomly.
Incorrect. Touton cells occur in xanthogranulomatous lesions with a foamy rim.
Correct. Peripheral horseshoe nuclei define Langhans giant cells.
Incorrect. Reed Sternberg cells are neoplastic cells of Hodgkin lymphoma.
items.kp: Horseshoe peripheral nuclei means Langhans giant cell.

items.q: Non-caseating granulomas in lung and hilar nodes with raised angiotensin converting enzyme most strongly suggest which condition?
items.exp: Sarcoidosis produces tight non-caseating granulomas along lymphatics with hilar adenopathy. Tuberculosis and fungal granulomas usually caseate, so exclusion of infection remains mandatory.
r: Incorrect. Tuberculosis typically caseates and needs microbiological exclusion.
Correct. Non-caseating granulomas with hilar nodes suggest sarcoidosis.
Incorrect. Histoplasmosis usually produces caseating granulomas.
Incorrect. Granulomatosis with polyangiitis causes necrotising vasculitis, not this pattern.
items.kp: Sarcoidosis is a diagnosis that still requires excluding infection.

items.q: Which cytokine is most important for classical macrophage activation and granuloma maintenance?
items.exp: Interferon gamma from T helper 1 cells classically activates macrophages and sustains granulomas. Tumour necrosis factor also maintains granuloma integrity, which explains tuberculosis reactivation with its blockade.
r: Incorrect. Interleukin 4 drives alternative activation and repair.
Incorrect. Interleukin 10 is mainly anti-inflammatory.
Correct. Interferon gamma drives classical activation and granulomas.
Incorrect. Transforming growth factor beta mainly drives fibrosis.
items.kp: Interferon gamma builds granulomas; anti-TNF therapy can break them.

items.q: Granulation tissue at a healing wound edge is best described as which combination?
o: New capillaries, fibroblasts and loose matrix
Mature dense collagen with few vessels
items.exp: Granulation tissue is early repair tissue with proliferating capillaries, fibroblasts and oedematous matrix. A granuloma is an organised macrophage collection, a different structure with a similar name.
r: Incorrect. That describes a granuloma, not granulation tissue.
Correct. Granulation tissue means new vessels, fibroblasts and loose matrix.
Incorrect. Dense mature collagen describes a later scar.
Incorrect. Neutrophils in debris describe an abscess.
items.kp: Never confuse granulation tissue with granuloma in exams.

items.q: A patient starting anti-tumour necrosis factor therapy reactivates latent tuberculosis. What is the mechanism?
items.exp: Tumour necrosis factor maintains granuloma structure that contains latent mycobacteria. Blocking it disorganises granulomas and allows reactivation, so screening before therapy is required.
r: Incorrect. Neutrophil burst defects cause different recurrent infections.
Correct. Granulomas need tumour necrosis factor to stay organised.
Incorrect. Antibody failure causes sinopulmonary bacterial infections.
Incorrect. Complement defects predispose to Neisseria infection.
items.kp: Screen for latent tuberculosis before anti-TNF treatment.

items.q: Which pairing of granuloma type and cause is correct?
o: Foreign body granuloma and viral infection
items.exp: Tuberculosis classically produces caseating granulomas, while sarcoidosis produces non-caseating granulomas. Foreign body reactions surround inert material such as suture or talc.
r: Incorrect. Sarcoidosis is typically non-caseating.
Incorrect. Tuberculosis is typically caseating.
Correct. Tuberculosis pairs with caseating granulomas.
Incorrect. Foreign body granulomas surround inert material, not viruses.

items.q: Epithelioid cells within a granuloma are derived from which precursor?
items.exp: Epithelioid cells are activated macrophages with abundant pale cytoplasm resembling epithelial cells. They secrete angiotensin converting enzyme and form the core of granulomas.
r: Incorrect. Lymphocytes form the rim, not the epithelioid core.
Correct. Epithelioid cells are activated macrophages.
Incorrect. Fibroblasts deposit collagen around lesions.
Incorrect. Endothelial cells line vessels and do not form granuloma cores.
items.kp: Epithelioid means macrophage derived, despite the name.

items.q: Schistosome eggs in bladder tissue provoke which type of inflammatory response?
items.exp: Helminth eggs are large persistent antigens that provoke granulomatous inflammation with eosinophils. Chronic bladder involvement is linked to fibrosis and increased squamous carcinoma risk.
r: Incorrect. Abscesses follow pyogenic bacteria, not helminth eggs.
Correct. Persistent eggs provoke granulomatous inflammation.
Incorrect. Serous inflammation is fluid rich and transient.
Incorrect. Fibrinous patterns describe serosal surfaces such as pericardium.
items.kp: Parasite eggs and granulomas are a classic exam pairing.
